images.title: Theodore Roosevelt, 1903 portrait by John Singer Sargent
images.description: John Singer Sargent's 1903 oil portrait of Theodore Roosevelt, the president of the Square Deal.

images.title: Upton Sinclair, author of The Jungle
images.description: Studio portrait of novelist Upton Sinclair, whose 1906 novel The Jungle exposed Chicago's meatpacking plants.

images.title: Cover of Upton Sinclair's novel The Jungle (1906)
images.description: First-edition cover of The Jungle, the 1906 novel whose meatpacking horrors pushed Congress to pass food-safety laws.

images.title: Cattle pens at the Chicago stockyards, 1909
images.description: Cattle pens at Chicago's Union Stock Yards in 1909, the meatpacking world Upton Sinclair exposed in The Jungle.

images.title: The Appeal to Reason office, Girard, Kansas
images.description: The Kansas office of the Appeal to Reason, the socialist weekly that first serialized Sinclair's The Jungle in 1905.

images.title: Federal food and drug inspectors at work, 1909
images.description: Federal inspectors enforcing the 1906 Pure Food and Drug Act, a direct result of The Jungle's public outrage.

images.title: Lydia Pinkham's Vegetable Compound advertisement
images.description: Advertisement for Lydia Pinkham's Vegetable Compound, the kind of patent medicine the 1906 Pure Food and Drug Act forced to label honestly.

images.title: Ida Tarbell, muckraking journalist
images.description: Portrait of Ida Tarbell, whose McClure's investigation of Standard Oil became the classic muckraking exposé.

images.title: S. S. McClure, founder of McClure's Magazine
images.description: S. S. McClure, whose magazine fed middle-class hunger for muckraking exposés like Tarbell's Standard Oil series.

images.title: Standard Oil as an octopus, Puck magazine 1904
images.description: Udo Keppler's 1904 Puck centerfold 'Next!' picturing Standard Oil as an octopus strangling the steel, copper, and shipping industries.

images.title: An oil refinery, circa 1900
images.description: An American oil refinery around 1900, the industry Ida Tarbell exposed for secret railroad rebates and strong-arm buyouts.

images.title: Lincoln Steffens, muckraker of city corruption
images.description: Portrait of Lincoln Steffens, author of The Shame of the Cities, the muckraking exposé of urban political machines.

images.title: The Shame of the Cities by Lincoln Steffens (1904)
images.description: Cover of The Shame of the Cities, Steffens's 1904 book exposing corruption in American city governments.

images.title: Jacob Riis, photographer of New York's tenements
images.description: Portrait of Jacob Riis, whose flash photographs of tenement life powered How the Other Half Lives (1890).

images.title: Bandit's Roost, Mulberry Street, photographed by Jacob Riis (1888)
images.description: Jacob Riis's 1888 flash photograph of Bandit's Roost on Mulberry Street, New York's most notorious tenement alley.

images.title: Children photographed by Jacob Riis
images.description: New York street children photographed by Jacob Riis, the visual evidence behind How the Other Half Lives.

images.title: Tenement street on New York's Lower East Side, early 1900s
images.description: A crowded Lower East Side street in the early 1900s, the immigrant neighborhoods the muckrakers documented.

images.title: Breaker boys at a Pennsylvania coal breaker, photographed by Lewis Hine
images.description: Lewis Hine's photograph of breaker boys picking slate at a Pennsylvania coal breaker, child labor in the Gilded Age.

images.title: Child spinner in a Georgia cotton mill, photographed by Lewis Hine
images.description: Lewis Hine's photograph of a young spinner in a Georgia cotton mill, part of his campaign against child labor.

images.title: Child newsboys in St. Louis, 1910, photographed by Lewis Hine
images.description: Lewis Hine's 1910 photograph of child newsboys in St. Louis, documenting children as young as ten working city streets.

images.title: Andrew Carnegie
images.description: Andrew Carnegie, the steel magnate whose trust-era industry the progressives sought to regulate.

images.title: Richard Croker, Tammany Hall boss
images.description: Richard Croker, boss of New York's Tammany Hall machine, which traded jobs for votes.

images.title: Jane Addams, founder of Hull House
images.description: Portrait of Jane Addams, who opened Hull House in a Chicago immigrant neighborhood in 1889.

images.title: Hull House, Chicago settlement house
images.description: Hull House, the Chicago settlement Jane Addams opened in 1889, where reformers lived among the poor and ran kindergartens and clinics.

images.title: Hull House, Chicago (Library of Congress)
images.description: Hull House in Chicago, the settlement where Jane Addams's model of kindergartens and health clinics spread to four hundred houses.

images.title: Washington Gladden, Social Gospel minister
images.description: Washington Gladden, the minister who preached the Social Gospel: true faith fixed slums as well as saving souls.

images.title: William U'Ren, father of Oregon's initiative system
images.description: William U'Ren, the Oregon reformer behind the initiative, referendum, and recall tools that let citizens route around the machines.

images.title: A New York polling place, 1900
images.description: A New York polling place in 1900, the curtained-booth era of the secret ballot Massachusetts adopted in 1888.

images.title: Robert M. La Follette, 'Fighting Bob' of Wisconsin
images.description: Portrait of Wisconsin governor Robert La Follette, whose Wisconsin Idea brought university professors into government to draft reform laws.

images.title: The U.S. Senate chamber, 1910s
images.description: The U.S. Senate chamber in the 1910s; the Seventeenth Amendment (1913) took the choice of senators from legislatures and gave it to voters.

images.title: Senator Charles Curtis, 1913
images.description: Senator Charles Curtis in 1913, serving in the Senate the year the Seventeenth Amendment gave voters the direct election of senators.

images.title: Galveston after the 1900 hurricane
images.description: Galveston, Texas after the 1900 hurricane, the disaster that brought the commission form of government: trained managers instead of bosses.

images.title: The Temple of Music at the Pan-American Exposition, 1901
images.description: The Temple of Music at Buffalo's Pan-American Exposition, where President McKinley was assassinated in 1901, putting Theodore Roosevelt in the White House.

images.title: The Pan-American Exposition, Buffalo, 1901
images.description: The Pan-American Exposition in Buffalo, 1901, the fair where McKinley's assassination made the forty-two-year-old Theodore Roosevelt president.

images.title: Puck cartoon of President Roosevelt, 1904
images.description: A 1904 Puck cartoon of Theodore Roosevelt, preaching from the presidency he called his bully pulpit.

images.title: Anthracite coal miners during the 1902 strike
images.description: Anthracite miners during the 1902 coal strike, when Roosevelt threatened to send the Army to run the mines and forced owners to bargain.

images.title: Pennsylvania coal miners with a mule team
images.description: Pennsylvania coal miners posed around a mule hauling coal cars, the men whose 1902 strike Roosevelt intervened in.

images.title: James J. Hill, railroad magnate
images.description: James J. Hill, the railroad magnate behind the Northern Securities trust Roosevelt broke up in 1904.

images.title: A railroad yard, early 20th century
images.description: A railroad yard in the early 1900s, the industry the Hepburn Act of 1906 gave Washington real power to regulate.

images.title: E. H. Harriman, railroad magnate
images.description: E. H. Harriman, Hill's partner in the Northern Securities railroad trust, broken up with the Supreme Court's backing in 1904.

images.title: John D. Rockefeller, 1911
images.description: John D. Rockefeller in 1911, the year the Supreme Court broke up his Standard Oil in Taft's headline antitrust suit.

images.title: William Howard Taft, portrait by the Pach Brothers
images.description: Cabinet-card portrait of William Howard Taft, the quiet trust-buster who filed ninety antitrust suits, including the one that broke up Standard Oil.

images.title: Dr. Harvey Wiley, crusader for pure food
images.description: Dr. Harvey Wiley, the chemist whose campaign made the 1906 Pure Food and Drug Act possible.

images.title: Yosemite Valley, early 1900s
images.description: Yosemite Valley in the early 1900s, part of the conservation estate Roosevelt built: five new national parks and over two hundred million acres set aside.

images.title: Gifford Pinchot, first chief of the U.S. Forest Service
images.description: Gifford Pinchot in 1909, Roosevelt's forestry chief, who said forests should be used wisely so they last.

images.title: John Muir, naturalist and preservationist
images.description: Naturalist John Muir, circa 1880, who said wild places should be left alone, clashing with Pinchot over Hetch Hetchy.

images.title: Theodore Roosevelt and John Muir at Glacier Point, Yosemite, 1903
images.description: Theodore Roosevelt and John Muir at Glacier Point, Yosemite, in 1903, the camping trip that cemented Roosevelt's conservation crusade.

images.title: Hetch Hetchy Valley, Yosemite
images.description: Hetch Hetchy Valley in Yosemite, the valley John Muir fought to save and San Francisco dammed in 1913.

images.title: Hetch Hetchy Dam under construction
images.description: The Hetch Hetchy dam under construction, the 1913 defeat of Muir's preservationists in their war with Pinchot's conservationists.

images.title: Bull Moose campaign cartoon, 1912
images.description: A 1912 campaign cartoon for Roosevelt's Progressive Bull Moose Party, the split that handed the election to Wilson.

images.title: 1912 campaign cartoon: Roosevelt, Wilson, and Taft
images.description: A 1912 campaign cartoon picturing Theodore Roosevelt, Woodrow Wilson, and William Howard Taft, the four-way race Wilson won with forty-one percent.

images.title: Roosevelt on the stump, 1912
images.description: Theodore Roosevelt campaigning in 1912 after walking out of the Republican convention.

images.title: Eugene Debs, Socialist presidential candidate
images.description: Portrait of Eugene Debs, the Socialist candidate who won six percent of the vote in the 1912 election.

images.title: Woodrow Wilson, 1913
images.description: Woodrow Wilson in 1913, the president of the New Freedom, who wanted to break up bigness and restore competition.

images.title: Samuel Gompers, AFL leader
images.description: Samuel Gompers, the labor leader whose unions the Clayton Act took off the antitrust target list.

images.title: The Federal Trade Commission headquarters, Washington
images.description: The Federal Trade Commission's headquarters in Washington, the watchdog over unfair business practices created in 1914.

images.title: Carter Glass, author of the Federal Reserve Act
images.description: Carter Glass, the congressman who authored the Federal Reserve Act of 1913, creating twelve regional banks.

images.title: The floor of the New York Stock Exchange
images.description: The floor of the New York Stock Exchange, photographed in secret, in the era when the Panic of 1907 showed the system resting on one private banker, J.P. Morgan.

images.title: J.P. Morgan with his family
images.description: J.P. Morgan with his family, the private banker the whole system rested on during the Panic of 1907.

images.title: Poster for The Birth of a Nation (1915)
images.description: Poster for D.W. Griffith's The Birth of a Nation (1915), the racist film glorifying the Ku Klux Klan that President Wilson praised.

images.title: Still from The Birth of a Nation (1915)
images.description: A still from The Birth of a Nation, the 1915 film whose glorification of the Klan exposed progressivism's racial blind spot.

images.title: W.E.B. Du Bois, portrait by Winold Reiss (1925)
images.description: Winold Reiss's 1925 pastel portrait of W.E.B. Du Bois, who demanded full political equality with no patience and no compromise.

images.title: The Niagara Movement meets, Fort Erie, 1905
images.description: The Niagara Movement's 1905 meeting at Fort Erie, Canada, where Du Bois demanded full political equality.

images.title: Booker T. Washington with Theodore Roosevelt at Tuskegee
images.description: Booker T. Washington with Theodore Roosevelt at Tuskegee Institute, the economic-progress-first answer to Du Bois.

images.title: Students building at Tuskegee Institute
images.description: Students doing roof construction at Tuskegee Institute, Washington's school for Black economic self-improvement.

images.title: Marcus Garvey
images.description: Portrait of Marcus Garvey, whose back-to-Africa movement offered a third answer for Black Americans in the Progressive Era.

images.title: Alice Paul, suffragist leader
images.description: Portrait of Alice Paul, founder of the National Woman's Party (1916), whose parades, hunger strikes, and civil disobedience pushed Wilson to back suffrage.

images.title: Carrie Chapman Catt, NAWSA leader
images.description: Portrait of Carrie Chapman Catt, leader of the National American Woman Suffrage Association, two million members strong by 1917.

images.title: Suffragists picketing the White House, 1917
images.description: National Woman's Party suffragists picketing the White House in 1917, the radical tactics that helped win the Nineteenth Amendment.

images.title: Woman suffrage parade, New York City, 1915
images.description: A woman suffrage parade in New York City on October 23, 1915, part of the mass movement that won the vote in 1920.

images.title: Tennessee's certification of the 19th Amendment, 1920
images.description: Tennessee's 1920 certification ratifying the Nineteenth Amendment, the final state needed to enfranchise women.

images.title: William McAdoo, Secretary of the Treasury
images.description: William McAdoo, the Treasury secretary who implemented the 1913 income tax under the Sixteenth Amendment.

images.title: Wayne Wheeler, Anti-Saloon League lobbyist
images.description: Wayne Wheeler, the Anti-Saloon League lobbyist who drove the Eighteenth Amendment's 1919 ban on alcohol.

images.title: Frances Willard, WCTU leader
images.description: Frances Willard, the longtime leader of the Woman's Christian Temperance Union behind the prohibition push.
